smell: Two concurrent `okdctl deploy` or `okdctl destroy` invocations in the same project root both point at `infrastructure/terraform/environments/<env>/terraform.tfstate` with no Go-side barrier. Terraform itself takes a local-backend lock only around individual sub-commands (init/plan/apply/destroy each relock), so a race between okdctl run A's plan step and run B's destroy step is not protected end-to-end. Nothing in okdctl's own orchestrator checks 'am I the only okdctl running?' — no pidfile, no flock, no stale-run detection.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — concurrent runs on the same state file can interleave at any terraform command boundary and corrupt state. Mitigated by single-operator discipline but not enforced.
fix_summary: Acquire a flock on `<workDir>/.okdctl.lock` at orchestrator entry (deploy/destroy/cleanup/update-ingress). Release on orchestrator exit. On contention, fail fast with 'another okdctl run is active (pid=N, started=T)' instead of racing. Use `github.com/gofrs/flock` (BSD-licensed, no transitive weight). The lock is orthogonal to terraform's own lock — it prevents two okdctl orchestrators from interleaving at step boundaries.
rule_source: Terraform local-backend docs (per-command lock, not per-orchestration lock)
Go proverb: 'do not communicate by sharing memory; share memory by communicating' — single-writer invariant
must_preserve: existing terraform.Executor API; single-operator usage pattern

smell: StepDef has no 'already-done' precondition hook or checkpoint. If okdctl crashes mid-setup (e.g. after building ISOs but before uploading), the next run starts from step 1, repeating work or reconciling side-effects ad-hoc. Each step's idempotency is implicit — some steps check FileExists (setup/artifacts.go), others re-run unconditionally (GenerateManifests, Inject*). There is no declared `ReRunSafe bool` field on StepDef and no on-disk checkpoint recording 'last-completed-step-id' that the next orchestrator run can skip to. InterruptSummary (cli/summary.go) tells the user 'resume with okdctl deploy' but the resume simply re-runs from step 0.
evidence:
type StepDef struct {
    ID         StepID
    Name       string
    Desc       string
    NonFatal   bool
    SkipWhen   func() bool
    SkipReason string
    OnStart    func()
    Exec       func(ctx context.Context) error
    OnError    func(error)
}
severity_reason: Not blocker — re-running deploy is mostly harmless because most steps happen to be idempotent, but the implicit-idempotency contract is fragile. Upgrades to the 40-step phase graph risk introducing a non-idempotent step that silently corrupts a partial deploy.
fix_summary: Option A (lightweight): add `ReRunSafe bool` on StepDef, default false, and require every StepDef to declare it (compile-fail via lint if a step sets Fatal without setting ReRunSafe explicitly). Document the contract in step.go. Option B (heavier): add on-disk checkpoint at `<workDir>/.okdctl-progress.json` — StepResult list after each step, skipped on re-run when step.ID matches. Start with A — cheap, forces authors to think about idempotency at the StepDef level.
rule_source: Twelve-factor §disposability (processes should be resilient to crashes)
repo-counter-example: roadmap.md mentions N10 'Ctrl-C partial-progress summary' shipped but no resume semantic
must_preserve: StepDef + BuildSteps canonical API; backward compat for existing StepDefs

smell: destroySteps is all-or-nothing. Options expose SkipTerraform / SkipCleanup / SkipFirewall / KeepISOs as separate booleans, but there is no user-facing CLI flag to scope — `okdctl destroy` always runs the full graph. Operators who want 'destroy only VMs but keep haproxy/dnsmasq/firewall for debug' or 'destroy only files, infra is already gone' cannot express that without editing code or running `okdctl cleanup` as a separate command (which has its own issues — cleanup.Execute covers Full / WorkOnly / WebOnly / HAProxyOnly / TerraformOnly but destroy doesn't thread a --scope flag to it).
severity_reason: Feature-gap, not correctness. Workaround exists (run `okdctl cleanup` with its richer Kind enum). The destroy-side scoping just isn't exposed.
fix_summary: Add --scope=full|infra|files|firewall (default: full) and --skip-firewall / --skip-cleanup flags on destroyCmd, routing to the existing Options fields. Promote the cleanup.Kind enum so destroyCmd can accept the same scope names users already know from `okdctl cleanup`.
rule_source: roadmap.md N4 (okdctl cleanup standalone) demonstrates scoped teardown works; destroy should match its vocabulary
must_preserve: default behavior (full destroy on no flag)

smell: CleanupBootstrap creates `bootstrap-destroy.tfplan` via tf.Plan, then applies it, and only calls SafeRemove on the plan file on the success path. If tf.Apply fails, the plan file persists in the terraform dir. terraform.Executor.Cleanup (terraform.go:335) removes only `tfplan` / `destroy.tfplan` / `terraform.tfstate.backup` — not `bootstrap-destroy.tfplan`. A subsequent re-run of postinstall will plan again and overwrite the stale file, but a following `terraform` CLI inspection by the operator sees a stale plan that doesn't match current state.
severity_reason: Low-impact — a stray `bootstrap-destroy.tfplan` doesn't corrupt anything and next run overwrites it. Logged as a recovery hygiene issue, not a safety one.
fix_summary: Use `defer system.SafeRemove(planPath)` right after tf.Plan succeeds so the plan is removed regardless of Apply outcome. Or add 'bootstrap-destroy.tfplan' to terraform.Executor.Cleanup's file list.

smell: StepPrintSummary logs 'destroy: cluster teardown completed' unconditionally at end of the pipeline. Now that StepDestroyInfra is NonFatal=true (resolved state:366b3f2d), the orchestrator runs all cleanup steps even when terraform destroy failed, so this summary line now trips more often — it fires even when VMs still exist in Proxmox. Operator reading logs thinks 'we're clean'. StepResult slice in orchestrator.Results() has the truth, but the summary step doesn't inspect it — it just prints a fixed string.
severity_reason: Observability-into-data-loss gap: combined with state:366b3f2d's fix (infra step is now NonFatal) the summary can now claim 'teardown completed' when the cluster is still running. Previously the orchestrator aborted before reaching this step on TF failure — resolving state:366b3f2d promoted this from minor to major.
fix_summary: Have StepPrintSummary inspect orchestrator.Results() (or accept a PhaseContext with step outcomes) and render the same structured box summary.InterruptSummary uses — one row per step with ok/fail/skip status. If any step failed, emit 'destroy: teardown completed with N warning(s); VMs may still exist — see log above' instead of an unconditional success line. This is the downstream half of the state:366b3f2d fix.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/cli/summary.go InterruptSummary already has the pattern for per-step ok/fail rendering
seam: destroy-safety co-owned with audit-security (state-and-recovery owns recoverability / user-facing outcome surfacing)

smell: postinstall steps (cleanup-bootstrap, deploy-production-dns) are NonFatal and mutate cluster-external state (bootstrap VM destroyed via targeted tf apply, /etc/dnsmasq.d/*.conf replaced). If StepCleanupBootstrap succeeds but StepVerifyKubeVIP fails and StepDeployProductionDNS is skipped, the cluster is left with: bootstrap VM gone, kube-vip not verified, DNS still pointed at bootstrap. The user has no resume command specific to 'just the postinstall DNS step'. The destroy path will cope, but an operator trying to recover a stuck deploy has to hand-edit dnsmasq configs or re-run full deploy. update-ingress (cli/update_ingress.go) handles the haproxy->LB-IP transition, not the bootstrap->kube-vip DNS swap this scenario needs.
severity_reason: Design debt not correctness bug: the staged NonFatal approach is intentional (degrade-gracefully to haproxy routing when kube-vip fails) but the resume story for 'finish postinstall DNS when kube-vip comes up later' is not documented and has no dedicated CLI path. `okdctl update-ingress` covers a different scenario (haproxy->LB-IP).
fix_summary: Two options: (a) add `okdctl postinstall --step=dns` subcommand that re-runs just the DNS sub-phase once kube-vip is confirmed healthy; or (b) expand update-ingress to handle the bootstrap->production DNS transition when it's still pointing at bootstrap IP. Prefer (b) since update-ingress already owns DNS re-deploys.
must_preserve: postinstall step ordering; NonFatal semantics that let partial success still give a usable cluster

smell: Provider.Provision delegates 100% to terraform — no Go-side retry on transient Proxmox API failures, no 409-already-exists handling beyond what the bpg/proxmox provider does internally. retrieveProvisionResult derives VM IPs from config (not from Proxmox), so eventual-consistency 'VM created but not yet listed' gaps are dodged by not querying Proxmox — but any future code that enumerates VMs from the API will need retry. The warn log at proxmox.go:172 'run okdctl destroy to clean up' is the only recovery guidance on apply failure. The only direct Proxmox API use in the codebase is the wizard discovery path (internal/tui/wizard/steps/proxmox_discovery.go) which is read-only and out-of-band from deploy/destroy.
severity_reason: Currently no direct Proxmox API calls from Go on the deploy/destroy path (the provider is pure-terraform), so there's nothing to retry. Filed as a forward-looking note for when any future code paths query Proxmox directly (e.g. status checks that don't go through terraform output).
fix_summary: Document the invariant in proxmox.go header: 'All Proxmox mutation MUST go through terraform.Executor. Direct HTTP calls are forbidden on deploy/destroy.' If/when status queries are added, use internal/download's retry helper (5xx/408/429 with exponential backoff, 4xx fail-fast) which is already justified for HTTP retries.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/download/retry.go (established retry pattern in repo per roadmap U3)
